g_rules.rule: When generating search terms, expand all medical abbreviations to their full clinical terms using standard medical nomenclature, then include both the abbreviation and expansion in the search query to maximize recall

For findings and disorders, prefer concepts that match the clinical polarity (positive/negative) of the original text - if text indicates absence or negation, still link to the positive concept unless a specific negative concept exists

When multiple hierarchy types are available for the same clinical concept, prioritize based on context: procedures for actions/interventions, findings for observations/states, disorders for pathological conditions
Consider section context when interpreting ambiguous terms - abbreviations and terms may have different meanings in Physical Exam vs other sections

stage_1_span.label: Physical_Exam_Abbreviation
stage_1_span.description: Single capital letters or short uppercase abbreviations in Physical Exam sections that represent examination systems or clinical findings (e.g., VS, CV, PULM, ABD, NAD, RRR, CTAB)

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Expand abbreviations to their medical examination equivalents: VS to vital signs, CV to cardiovascular examination, PULM to pulmonary/respiratory examination, ABD to abdominal examination, then search for both abbreviation and expanded terms

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: In Physical Exam context, prioritize examination procedures for system abbreviations (CV, PULM, ABD) and finding concepts for result abbreviations (NAD, RRR, CTAB)

stage_1_span.label: Clinical_Condition
stage_1_span.description: Disease names, medical conditions, and pathological states including compound terms like 'biliary pancreatitis' or 'pancreatic necrosis'

stage_2_search.filtering_logic: Drop if preceded by 'No history of' or similar strong negation phrases indicating absence
stage_2_search.intent_translation: Search for the exact condition name, but also include common clinical synonyms (e.g., biliary pancreatitis should also search for gallstone pancreatitis)

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Prefer disorder concepts over finding concepts for pathological conditions; for compound conditions, select the most specific matching concept

stage_1_span.label: Medical_Procedure
stage_1_span.description: Surgical procedures, medical interventions, therapeutic actions, and clinical management activities

stage_2_search.intent_translation: For descriptive phrases, extract the core procedure (e.g., 'surgical resection of your gallbladder' becomes 'cholecystectomy'); for action verbs, expand to full procedure names

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Prioritize procedure concepts; when multiple specificity levels exist, choose based on available clinical detail (laparoscopic cholecystectomy over general cholecystectomy if laparoscopic is specified)

stage_1_span.label: Clinical_Finding
stage_1_span.description: Observable patient states, clinical signs, symptoms, and examination results including both normal and abnormal findings

stage_2_search.intent_translation: For negative prefixes (afebrile), search for the positive concept (fever); for descriptive phrases, extract the clinical finding essence

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select finding concepts that match the clinical observation; for negative prefixes, choose the positive concept unless a specific negative finding exists

stage_1_span.label: Anatomical_Structure
stage_1_span.description: Body parts, organs, anatomical regions, and structural references

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Use standard anatomical terminology; for abbreviations like 'GI tract', expand to full anatomical name

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select body structure concepts; prefer structure concepts over finding or procedure concepts

examples: GI tract -> Gastrointestinal tract structure (body structure)

stage_1_span.label: Medication_Allergy
stage_1_span.description: Drug names or drug classes mentioned in allergy sections

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Transform drug name to allergy finding by searching for 'allergy to [drug name]' pattern

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select allergy finding concepts that include the specific drug or drug class

stage_1_span.label: Contextual_Abbreviation
stage_1_span.description: Abbreviations whose meaning depends on clinical context (e.g., RA can mean room air or rheumatoid arthritis)

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Expand based on section and surrounding context: RA in vital signs context means 'room air breathing', in rheumatology means 'rheumatoid arthritis'

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Use section header and surrounding clinical context to select appropriate concept expansion

stage_1_span.label: Implicit_Concept_Mapping
stage_1_span.description: Clinical phrases that map to semantically related but not literally matching SNOMED concepts

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Identify the clinical intent and search for the standard medical concept (e.g., 'pancreatic rest' refers to resting the pancreas, search for pancreatic-related concepts)

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select concepts based on clinical semantic similarity rather than literal text matching; consider the medical intent

stage_1_span.label: Activity_Status
stage_1_span.description: Descriptions of patient mobility, functional status, and activity levels

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Convert activity descriptions to standard functional status terms (ambulatory, independent, mobile)

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Select finding concepts that describe functional or activity status

stage_1_span.label: Educational_Instruction
stage_1_span.description: Patient education activities, discharge instructions, and therapeutic guidance

stage_2_search.intent_translation: Transform instructional phrases into education or training procedure concepts

stage_3_select.disambiguation_logic: Prefer education or training procedures over general procedure concepts
